q-1471.name: Question 1
q-1471.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $A⇔B$ is true if $A⇒B$ **and** $B⇒A.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $A⇔B$ is true if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So in this case, we have

$$
P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P).
$$

q-107158.name: Question 2
q-107158.worked_solution:
First, we use the definition of the biconditional statement to write the equivalence as a conjunction of implications: 

$$
¬A⇔B≡(¬A⇒B)∧(B⇒¬A)
$$

Now, we represent all the implications using disjunctions and negations:

$$
(¬A⇒B)∧(B⇒¬A)≡(¬¬A∨B)∧(¬B∨¬A)
$$

Next, we use De Morgan's laws:

$$
(¬¬A∨B)∧(¬B∨¬A)≡(¬¬A∨B)∧¬(B∧A)
$$

Finally, we simplify the double negations:

$$
(¬¬A∨B)∧¬(B∧A)≡(A∨B)∧¬(B∧A)
$$

q-107221.name: Question 3
q-107221.problem:
$$
¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧
$$

What expression should be inserted into the blank space above to give logically equivalent statements?
q-107221.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $A⇔B$ is true if $A⇒B$ **and** $B⇒A.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $A⇔B$ is true if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So, in this case, we have

$$
¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧[\,Y⇒¬(Y∧X)].
$$

Therefore, the missing part is $Y⇒¬(Y∧X).$

q-107221.html:
Question 3
?

¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧AAAAAAAAAA

What expression should be inserted into the blank space above to give logically equivalent statements?

a
 Y⇒¬(Y∧X)
b
¬(Y∧X)⇒Y
c
 Y⇒(Y∧X)
d
¬Y⇒(Y∧X)
e
¬(Y∧X)⇒¬Y
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

According to the definition of the biconditional,

  • A⇔B is true if A⇒B and B⇒A. Otherwise, it is false.

  • In other words, A⇔B is true if A and B have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So, in this case, we have

¬(Y∧X)⇔Y≡[¬(Y∧X)⇒Y]∧[Y⇒¬(Y∧X)].

Therefore, the missing part is Y⇒¬(Y∧X).

q-182523.name: Question 4
q-182523.worked_solution:
First, we use the definition of the biconditional statement to write the equivalence as a conjunction of implications: 

$$
¬(Y⇔X)≡¬[(Y⇒X)∧(X⇒Y)]
$$

Now, we represent all the implications using disjunctions and negations:

$$
¬[(Y⇒X)∧(X⇒Y)]≡¬[(¬Y∨X)∧(¬X∨Y)]
$$

Next, we use De Morgan's laws:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬[(¬Y∨X)∧(¬X∨Y)] & ≡¬(¬Y∨X)∨¬(¬X∨Y) \\  & ≡(¬¬Y∧¬X)∨(¬¬X∧¬Y)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the double negations:

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬¬Y∧¬X)∨(¬¬X∧¬Y) & ≡(Y∧¬X)∨(X∧¬Y)\end{aligned}
$$

q-182523.html:
Question 4
?

¬(Y⇔X)≡

a
(Y∧X)∨(¬X∧¬Y)
b
¬X∧Y
c
X∧¬Y
d
(Y∧¬X)∧(X∧¬Y)
e
(Y∧¬X)∨(X∧¬Y)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we use the definition of the biconditional statement to write the equivalence as a conjunction of implications: ¬(Y⇔X)≡¬[(Y⇒X)∧(X⇒Y)]

Now, we represent all the implications using disjunctions and negations: ¬[(Y⇒X)∧(X⇒Y)]≡¬[(¬Y∨X)∧(¬X∨Y)]

Next, we use De Morgan's laws:

¬[(¬Y∨X)∧(¬X∨Y)]≡¬(¬Y∨X)∨¬(¬X∨Y)≡(¬¬Y∧¬X)∨(¬¬X∧¬Y)

Finally, we simplify the double negations: (¬¬Y∧¬X)∨(¬¬X∧¬Y)≡(Y∧¬X)∨(X∧¬Y)

q-182580.name: Question 5
q-182580.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,¬(X∨Y)⇔X\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
q-182580.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $P⇔Q$ is true if $P⇒Q$ **and** $Q⇒P.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $P⇔Q$ is true if $P$ and $Q$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

First, we add a columns for $X∨Y$ and $¬(X∨Y):$

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,X∨Y\,$ | $\,¬(X∨Y)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $¬(X∨Y)⇔X.$ 

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,X∨Y\,$ | $\,¬(X∨Y)\,$ | $\,¬(X∨Y)⇔X\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
